newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Japan calls for closer NATO ties.
newsitem.headline: Japan calls for closer NATO ties.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda called on Tuesday for closer ties between his country and NATO, saying the alliance's imminent eastward expansion would also impact on Asia.
"We agreed today we will have even closer links and coordination between Japan and NATO," he told reporters after a brief meeting with the alliance's Secretary-General Javier Solana.

NATO is set next month to invite Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary -- and possibly even more former communist European countries -- to join the West's defence organisation at a special summit in Madrid.

Last month, the 16 members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) led by the United States signed a landmark post-Cold War treaty with Russia, known as the Founding Act, to meet Moscow's objections to enlargement.
"We shared the view that the enlargement of NATO and the Founding Act will have an enormous impact not only on Europe, but on Asia including Japan," Ikeda said.
But he added that such cooperation would remain at the "practical" level, indicating the relationship would not be formalised in some form of accord or partnership forum.
NATO and Japan have cooperated closely at the military level since the collapse of communism, mainly in northern Pacific waters off the old Soviet Union.

Eight Soviet submarines were destroyed under disarmament agreements at end of the Cold War and sunk in the Russian Arctic and Sea of Japan. NATO has helped Japan monitor radioactivity levels from them.
